The faiss-cpu PyPI package declares `packaging` as a required runtime dependency, per [PyPI package metadata](https://pypi.org/project/faiss-cpu/).
FAISS prefers Intel MKL as its BLAS/LAPACK backend when FAISS_ENABLE_MKL=ON (the default), though it is unavailable on riscv64 and CMake silently falls back to OpenBLAS, per the project report §9.1.
FAISS uses SWIG as a build-time-only Python wrapper code generator for its Python bindings, per the project report §9.3.
FAISS's GPU indexes optionally depend on CUDA/cuBLAS for GPU-accelerated search and training, entirely unavailable on riscv64, per the project report §9.2.

OpenBLAS's Dependencies table lists glibc as providing the C runtime, pthreads, libm, and the `riscv_hwprobe` syscall used for RISC-V runtime CPU-feature dispatch, per [project-reports/openblas.md §9](project-reports/openblas.md).

The report's Dependencies table lists GCC/GFortran as required for kernel code generation, with GFortran needed to compile the bundled netlib LAPACK and GCC 14+ specifically required to correctly generate RVV code for the ZVL128B/ZVL256B targets, per [project-reports/openblas.md §9](project-reports/openblas.md).

The Dependencies table lists Binutils/objcopy as needed for symbol renaming, linking, and assembling, supported for riscv64 since binutils 2.28+, per [project-reports/openblas.md §9](project-reports/openblas.md).

The Dependencies table lists pthreads as the SMP threading backend used when OpenBLAS is built with `USE_THREAD`, noted as bundled with glibc on riscv64, per [project-reports/openblas.md §9](project-reports/openblas.md).
The Dependencies table lists OpenMP (libgomp/libomp) as an optional threading backend enabled via `USE_OPENMP=1`, green on riscv64 per [project-reports/openblas.md §9](project-reports/openblas.md).

OpenBLAS bundles netlib LAPACK (Fortran-compiled by default, disabled via `NOFORTRAN=1`) to provide its LAPACK routines, though the report notes LAPACK correctness is not validated in upstream riscv64 CI, per [project-reports/openblas.md §9](project-reports/openblas.md).

The Dependencies table lists QEMU riscv64 as a CI-only (not runtime) dependency used for all riscv64 test execution, since no native riscv64 CI hardware exists upstream, per [project-reports/openblas.md §9](project-reports/openblas.md).

oneDNN's CPU engine defaults to `DNNL_CPU_RUNTIME=OMP` (OpenMP) for threading, per the project's [CMake build options](https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneDNN/blob/main/cmake/options.cmake) and [README build requirements](https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneDNN#requirements-for-building-from-source).
XNNPACK's [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/google/XNNPACK/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt) downloads and builds against `cpuinfo` for runtime CPU ISA/feature detection used to dispatch micro-kernels.
XNNPACK's [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/google/XNNPACK/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt) downloads and links `pthreadpool` as its thread-pool implementation for parallelizing operator execution.

FBGEMM statically links the asmjit JIT assembler as a git submodule and uses it at build/runtime to generate optimized matrix-multiplication kernels, per [.gitmodules](https://github.com/pytorch/FBGEMM/blob/main/.gitmodules).

FBGEMM vendors Google/PyTorch's cpuinfo library as a git submodule to detect CPU ISA features (AVX2/AVX512) and select kernel variants, per [.gitmodules](https://github.com/pytorch/FBGEMM/blob/main/.gitmodules).

Pydantic's [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/pyproject.toml) lists `typing-extensions>=4.15.0` as a required runtime dependency, used for backported/advanced typing constructs.

Pydantic v2's [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/pyproject.toml) pins `pydantic-core==2.48.0` as a required runtime dependency — the Rust-implemented validation/serialization engine that the pure-Python `pydantic` package wraps, making it the single most load-bearing dependency of the project.
httpx's [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/master/pyproject.toml) declares `requires-python = ">=3.9"`, so it runs on and requires a CPython interpreter.

httpx's [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/master/pyproject.toml) lists `httpcore==1.*` as a core runtime dependency — httpcore is the low-level transport library httpx is built on top of, and is not one of the other stack nodes.

httpx's [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/master/pyproject.toml) lists `anyio` as a core dependency, providing its async/sync concurrency backend (asyncio and Trio support); it is not one of the other stack nodes.
aiohttp's [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/blob/master/pyproject.toml) lists `typing_extensions >= 4.4 ; python_version < '3.13'` as a direct runtime dependency.

aiohttp is a Python package (with C-accelerated extensions and CPython-only optional speedups like Brotli/aiodns) that needs a Python interpreter — CPython in this stack — installed and running to be usable at all, per its [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/blob/master/pyproject.toml) `requires-python >= 3.10` and platform_python_implementation checks.

aiohttp's HTTPS/TLS client and server support goes through Python's built-in `ssl` module, which is itself built against OpenSSL (1.1.1+), so secure connections are not usable without it, per [Python's ssl docs](https://docs.python.org/3/library/ssl.html) and aiohttp's [Advanced Client Usage](https://docs.aiohttp.org/en/stable/client_advanced.html) guide on SSL contexts.

typing_extensions is a pure-Python package with `requires-python = ">=3.9"` and no other runtime dependencies, per [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/python/typing_extensions/blob/main/pyproject.toml).

packaging is a pure-Python library with zero declared runtime dependencies ([`dependencies = []`](https://github.com/pypa/packaging/blob/main/pyproject.toml) in pyproject.toml) but needs a Python interpreter such as CPython (`requires-python >= "3.10"`) to be executed at all.

fsspec's `pyproject.toml` declares `http = ["aiohttp !=4.0.0a0, !=4.0.0a1"]` as an optional extra enabling `HTTPFileSystem`, per the [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/fsspec/filesystem_spec/blob/main/pyproject.toml).

fsspec's `pyproject.toml` lists `requests` as an optional dependency for the `github` and `dropbox` extras, per the [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/fsspec/filesystem_spec/blob/main/pyproject.toml).

fsspec's `pyproject.toml` declares a `tqdm = ["tqdm"]` optional extra used by its progress-callback utilities, per the [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/fsspec/filesystem_spec/blob/main/pyproject.toml).

tqdm's [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/tqdm/tqdm/blob/master/pyproject.toml) declares `requires-python = ">=3.8"` and no other in-stack runtime dependency, so CPython is the only stack node it explicitly needs to run.

NetworkX's `pyproject.toml` lists `numpy>=2` in the `default` optional-dependencies group, which most installs pull in via `pip install networkx[default]` for array-backed graph algorithms ([pyproject.toml](https://github.com/networkx/networkx/blob/main/pyproject.toml)).

The `extra` optional-dependencies group declares `sympy>=1.10`, used by NetworkX for symbolic computation in select algorithms ([pyproject.toml](https://github.com/networkx/networkx/blob/main/pyproject.toml)).

The `default` optional-dependencies group declares `scipy>=1.13`, which backs NetworkX's sparse-matrix and spectral graph algorithms (`networkx.linalg`) ([pyproject.toml](https://github.com/networkx/networkx/blob/main/pyproject.toml)).

NetworkX is a pure-Python package that declares `requires-python = '>=3.12,!=3.14.1'`, making a CPython interpreter mandatory to run it at all ([pyproject.toml](https://github.com/networkx/networkx/blob/main/pyproject.toml)).
sympy's [setup.py](https://github.com/sympy/sympy/blob/master/setup.py) requires Python >= 3.10 as its runtime interpreter.
sympy's [setup.py](https://github.com/sympy/sympy/blob/master/setup.py#L327-L329) declares `install_requires=['mpmath >= 1.1.0']`, its only required runtime package dependency.

The `opentelemetry-api` package's [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/blob/main/opentelemetry-api/pyproject.toml) declares a single runtime dependency, `typing-extensions >= 4.5.0`.

The API package ships only abstract classes and no-op implementations, so it produces no actual telemetry until an application installs and configures the [OpenTelemetry SDK](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/python/) to back it.

The `opentelemetry-sdk` package's [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/blob/main/opentelemetry-sdk/pyproject.toml) declares `opentelemetry-api == 1.45.0.dev` as a required dependency, since the SDK implements the API's provider interfaces.

The `opentelemetry-sdk` package's [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/blob/main/opentelemetry-sdk/pyproject.toml) declares `typing-extensions >= 4.5.0` as a required runtime dependency.
FlatBuffers optionally links [gRPC](https://github.com/grpc/grpc) solely to build the `FLATBUFFERS_BUILD_GRPCTEST` test target; it is not needed for production use of the library.
FlatBuffers pulls in [Protocol Buffers](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf) only transitively via the optional gRPC test target, not as a core dependency.
FlatBuffers pulls in [Abseil-cpp](https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp) only transitively via the optional gRPC test target, not as a core dependency.
The FlatBuffers Rust binding requires the [bitflags](https://crates.io/crates/bitflags) crate at runtime for flag/enum bitfield types.
The FlatBuffers Rust binding optionally depends on [serde](https://serde.rs/), feature-gated, as a serialization framework.

gRPC uses Protocol Buffers as its default wire serialization format and code generator (`protoc`), and lists it as a core dependency that builds on riscv64 but has no upstream prebuilt riscv64 `protoc` binary ([grpc.md](project-reports/grpc.md) Section 9.1/9.4).

gRPC can be built with `-DgRPC_SSL_PROVIDER=package` to substitute OpenSSL for the bundled BoringSSL, which is the recommended riscv64 mitigation since OpenSSL ships full riscv64 ISA coverage and Debian packages ([grpc.md](project-reports/grpc.md) Section 5 and 9.2).

BoringSSL is gRPC's default SSL/TLS and crypto provider, though on riscv64 it falls back entirely to scalar C code with no assembly optimizations or FIPS support ([grpc.md](project-reports/grpc.md) Section 4.1 and 9.2).

gRPC bundles abseil-cpp as a submodule for utilities, containers, and timing/hashing primitives, and has been affected by upstream abseil riscv64 issues (RDCYCLE removal causing SIGILL, open `-latomic` and SEGFAULT bugs) ([grpc.md](project-reports/grpc.md) Section 4.2 and 9.3).
gRPC depends on zlib for HTTP/2 message compression, which builds on riscv64 but with no SIMD acceleration ([grpc.md](project-reports/grpc.md) Section 9.1).
gRPC depends on c-ares for asynchronous DNS resolution, with no riscv64-specific issues noted ([grpc.md](project-reports/grpc.md) Section 9.1).
gRPC depends on Google's RE2 library for regular-expression matching, with no riscv64-specific issues noted ([grpc.md](project-reports/grpc.md) Section 9.1).

CPython links OpenSSL to implement the `_ssl` and `_hashlib` stdlib modules, and it builds on riscv64 with dedicated upstream CI ([openssl#30787](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/30787) tracks a riscv64 ChaCha20 RVV gap).

CPython's `_zstd` module (new in 3.14) links libzstd for compression, though its 4-way fast decompression loop isn't yet enabled on riscv64 ([zstd PR #4622](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4622)).
CPython's C runtime, pthreads, and math functions depend on glibc, which has had riscv64 support upstream since glibc 2.27.
libffi powers the `_ctypes` module for calling C functions from Python, and has open riscv64 issues including a struct-ABI test failure ([libffi#281](https://github.com/libffi/libffi/issues/281)).
zlib backs the stdlib `zlib` compression module and builds on riscv64 but with no SIMD acceleration path.
libbz2 backs the `_bz2` module and builds on riscv64 as pure C with no known issues.
liblzma backs the `_lzma` module; its riscv64 `FILTER_RISCV` constant gap was fixed in [PR #115989](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/115989), landing in 3.16.
libmpdec backs the `_decimal` module and builds on riscv64 via a generic uint128 fallback with no riscv64-specific assembly path.
libexpat backs the `pyexpat` and `_elementtree` modules and builds on riscv64 with no known issues.
SQLite backs the `_sqlite3` module and builds on riscv64 with no known issues.

mimalloc became CPython's default memory allocator in 3.13, and has open riscv64 hwprobe-based VA-space-detection PRs at [microsoft/mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc) affecting SV39 MMU hardware.
LLVM/Clang is the backend for CPython's Tier-2 `--enable-experimental-jit`, which is unsupported on riscv64 (`Tools/jit/_targets.py` raises `ValueError` for the platform).
glibc's Section 9 dependency table lists Python 3.4+ as required for the test harness scripts, available and passing on riscv64.
glibc requires GCC 12.1+ as its primary compiler (GCC 15+ specifically for RVV support), per the [glibc report](project-reports/glibc.md) Section 9 dependency table.
glibc requires GNU binutils 2.39+ for the assembler/linker, needing R_RISCV_ALIGN and R_RISCV_RELATIVE relocation support for static PIE on riscv64.
glibc requires Linux kernel headers 3.2+ (ARCH=riscv) to build the syscall ABI interface.
glibc's test suite exercises GDB 7.8+ pretty-printers, which are built for riscv64 but have known issues per the report.
glibc's static PIE probe uses eu-readelf from elfutils during testing/debugging, available and passing on riscv64.
glibc's Python-based test scripts pull in libffi as a runtime dependency of Python, with full riscv64 support.
glibc optionally links zlib (via libgd) for the memusagestat utility, available and passing tests on riscv64.
glibc optionally links libpng (via libgd) for the memusagestat utility, available and passing tests on riscv64.
glibc optionally links libcap to support SELinux capability handling in nscd, available and passing tests on riscv64.
glibc optionally links libselinux for nscd's SELinux support, available and passing tests on riscv64.
glibc optionally links libaudit for SELinux audit logging in nscd, available and passing tests on riscv64.
glibc requires GNU make 4.0+ to orchestrate its build system.
glibc requires GNU awk 3.1.2+ with MPFR for its build/test harness scripts.
glibc requires GNU bison 2.7+ for parser generation during the build.

OpenSSL depends on glibc as its runtime C library, including the `riscv_hwprobe` syscall used for ISA capability detection, per [Section 9 of the project report](https://github.com/openssl/openssl) (build/test/release all reported green on riscv64).

zstd is an optional dependency OpenSSL links for certificate compression; riscv64 decompression throughput is limited by an open [zstd riscv64 4-way-loop issue](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/issues/4622) that is not a correctness or build blocker.
OpenSSL's build system requires Perl 5 plus the Text::Template module to run the perlasm code generators, reported fully green on riscv64.
OpenSSL depends on the GNU assembler to assemble all perlasm-generated crypto `.S` files, requiring binutils >= 2.38 for Zvk vector-crypto instruction encoding.
zlib is an optional OpenSSL runtime dependency used for TLS compression, reported green across build/test/release on riscv64.
Brotli is an optional OpenSSL runtime dependency used for certificate compression, reported green across build/test/release on riscv64.

musl libc is an alternative runtime C library OpenSSL can build against, but riscv64 ISA-extension detection is broken on musl per [issue #28118](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/28118), silently disabling optimized code paths.

jemalloc requires glibc-provided pthreads (TLS, mutexes, background threads), libm (for `log(3)` when heap profiling is enabled), and libdl (`dlsym()` for lazy-lock multi-threading detection), as documented in [Section 9 of the jemalloc project report](https://github.com/jemalloc/jemalloc).

On riscv64, jemalloc requires GCC's libatomic runtime to emulate 8-bit/16-bit compare-exchange operations that the RISC-V A extension does not provide natively, auto-linked via the `-pthread` flag since [PR #1402](https://github.com/jemalloc/jemalloc/pull/1402).

tcmalloc depends on protobuf for profile proto serialization and the profile builder; riscv64 has no official protoc binary and downstream builds must build protobuf from source ([protobuf issue #12266](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/12266)).

glibc 2.35+'s own per-thread rseq registration conflicts with tcmalloc's rseq registration, tracked as open [tcmalloc issue #144](https://github.com/google/tcmalloc/issues/144), a prerequisite to resolve before per-CPU RSEQ caches (including on riscv64) can be safely enabled on glibc 2.35+ systems.

tcmalloc depends on abseil-cpp for logging, synchronization, CRC, hash tables, stack traces and the cycle clock, with open riscv64 sampler-test segfaults tracked in [abseil-cpp issue #2002](https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp/issues/2002).
re2 provides regular-expression matching, pulled in indirectly via abseil, with no known riscv64 build or test issues per the report's Section 9 table.

googletest is a test-only dependency that builds on riscv64, though `GetThreadCountTest.ReturnsCorrectValue` fails there per open [googletest issue #3756](https://github.com/google/googletest/issues/3756).
google/benchmark is a microbenchmark infrastructure dev dependency; a riscv64 sign-conversion warning was fixed via PR #1802 with no other known issues.
fuzztest is a fuzz-testing dev dependency with no known riscv64 build or test issues documented in the report.

tcmalloc's per-CPU RSEQ slab allocator depends on the Linux kernel's rseq syscall, available on riscv64 since kernel 4.18, though tcmalloc does not yet exercise it on that architecture ([rseq ABI docs](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/kernel/rseq.html)).

The report's Dependencies section lists glibc as LZ4's runtime dependency for `memcpy`/`memmove` and standard C functions, noting mature, unblocked riscv64 support (project-reports/lz4.md, Section 9).
LZ4 vendors a bundled snapshot of xxHash (v0.6.5, `lib/xxhash.c`) for content-integrity checksums in the lz4frame format, per the report's Dependencies section (project-reports/lz4.md, Section 9).
CMake is listed as an optional, build-time-only alternative build system for LZ4 requiring no riscv64-specific flags (project-reports/lz4.md, Section 9).

The project report's Dependencies section documents pthreads (part of glibc) as an optional dependency enabling `ZSTD_MULTITHREAD_SUPPORT`, corroborated by the Ubuntu `zstd` package's runtime dependency on `libc6` (see [packages.ubuntu.com/noble/zstd](https://packages.ubuntu.com/noble/zstd)).
The report lists LZ4 as an optional dependency used for `zlibWrapper` parity and contrib build targets, matching the Ubuntu `zstd` package's runtime dependency on `liblz4-1`.
The report documents zlib as an optional dependency that enables zstd's `zlibWrapper` drop-in-replacement build mode, matching the Ubuntu `zstd` package's runtime dependency on `zlib1g`.
The report documents liblzma/xz-utils as an optional dependency for legacy stream format support via `-DZSTD_LZMA_SUPPORT=ON`, matching the Ubuntu `zstd` package's runtime dependency on `liblzma5`.
The report notes xxhash is bundled directly into zstd's source tree (`lib/common/xxhash.c`) and used internally for XXH32/XXH64 content checksums.

Per [project-reports/snappy.md §9](https://github.com/google/snappy), LZ4 is an optional benchmark-comparison codec enabled via `HAVE_LIBLZ4` and is not a runtime dependency of the snappy library itself.
Per project-reports/snappy.md §9, zlib is an optional benchmark-comparison codec (`HAVE_LIBZ`) used only to compare compression performance, not a runtime dependency.
Per project-reports/snappy.md §9, LZO2 is an optional benchmark-comparison codec (`HAVE_LIBLZO2`) used only for benchmark comparisons, not a runtime dependency.
Per project-reports/snappy.md §9, [google/benchmark](https://github.com/google/benchmark) is vendored as the `third_party/benchmark` submodule and used as the build-time benchmarking framework.
Per project-reports/snappy.md §9, [google/googletest](https://github.com/google/googletest) is vendored as the `third_party/googletest` submodule and used as the build-time unit test framework.
